what: The ARDS lesson stops at the 2017 ATS/ESICM/SCCM guideline. The 2024 ATS update (Qadir et al., AJRCCM 2024) adds: corticosteroids (conditional for), higher PEEP without recruitment manoeuvres, a strong recommendation against prolonged recruitment manoeuvres, NMBA in early severe ARDS (conditional) and VV-ECMO in selected severe ARDS (conditional). The lesson cites Berlin 2012 but never defines ARDS (timing, bilateral opacities, P/F bands 300/200/100 on PEEP ≥ 5). The 2023 global definition (Matthay, AJRCCM 2024) adds SpO₂/FiO₂ and high-flow oxygen.
evidence: c10.js:36 and LSRC icu-ards. Source checked: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/5c98w95h (Qadir 2024 abstract).
fix: Add a "Definition" block (Berlin bands, plus a note on the 2023 global definition). Add bullets: corticosteroids (conditional, ATS 2024); "no prolonged recruitment manoeuvres (strong)". Add SRC qadir24 and matthay24 to LSRC icu-ards. Consider one question on steroids or recruitment manoeuvres.

what: PROSEVA figures are paired with "at least 12 h a day", but PROSEVA used sessions of at least 16 h. The "> 12 h" figure is the ATS 2017 recommendation. PROSEVA enrolment also required FiO₂ ≥ 0.6, PEEP ≥ 5, after 12–24 h of stabilisation.
fix: Reword to: "Prone for at least 12 h a day (ATS 2017; PROSEVA used ≥ 16 h) when P/F is below 150 on FiO₂ ≥ 0.6 and PEEP ≥ 5 (PROSEVA: 28-day mortality 16.0% vs 32.8%)."

what: Fever prevention applies to patients who remain comatose, and the temperature advice was updated in the 2022 ERC–ESICM temperature-control guideline after TTM2. The lesson gives no context on whether to cool to 32–36 °C.
evidence: c10.js:52 ("Prevent fever above 37.7 °C for at least 72 h"). Nolan 2021; Sandroni 2022 Intensive Care Med 48:261.
fix: Change to "In patients who remain comatose, prevent fever (above 37.7 °C) for at least 72 h", add "ERC–ESICM 2022: active fever prevention; no recommendation for routine cooling to 32–36 °C", and add sandroni22 to SRC/LSRC.

what: The explanation ignores the acute fall in HCO₃⁻ when PaCO₂ is lowered (the app's own rule is 2 per 10 for acute alkalosis), so the pH is overstated. The answer is still correct.
evidence: PaCO₂ 60 → 40 means HCO₃⁻ falls about 4 to 32, so pH = 6.1 + log(32/1.2) ≈ 7.53, not 7.58.
fix: Change the explanation to: "HCO₃⁻ stays near 36 (it falls only about 2–4 acutely): pH ≈ 7.53–7.58, a severe alkalosis."

what: "Disconnect and bag on 100% oxygen" has no caveat. In severe ARDS on high PEEP, disconnection derecruits the lung; use a bag with a PEEP valve, or a clamp, and minimise disconnections. This is not wrong for the exam, but it is incomplete for shift use.
fix: Add a line to the body: "On high PEEP (ARDS) use a PEEP valve on the bag and keep the disconnection brief."

what: The sources do not match the topics. Asthma ventilation is sourced only to BTS/ICS 2016 (a COPD/NIV hypercapnic-failure guideline) and Hickling. Adult ventilator troubleshooting is sourced only to APLS, a paediatric course.
fix: Add an asthma ventilation source, for example Leatherman J. Mechanical ventilation for severe asthma. Chest 2015;147:1671–1680 (verify the citation before adding). Add an adult source to icu-trouble (for example the ICS/FICM guidance or a critical care textbook chapter).

what: The EOLIA figure does not state its endpoint.
The wording differs slightly from SSC 2021, which says "at a dose of noradrenaline or adrenaline ≥ 0.25 µg/kg/min at least 4 h after initiation", with hydrocortisone typically 50 mg IV every 6 h.
fix: Reword to: "Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day (50 mg IV 6-hourly) when noradrenaline or adrenaline is still ≥ 0.25 µg/kg/min at least 4 h after starting."

what: SSC 2021 wording is "at least 30 mL/kg within the first 3 h"; the lesson says "about". The phrase "adjust for heart and kidney failure" is not in SSC and should be marked as clinical practice.
fix: Use "at least 30 mL/kg (SSC 2021, weak, low quality)" and "reassess often; be cautious in heart or kidney failure".

what: "Reduce the citrate dose" is right but vague; on a regional citrate circuit the citrate dose is tied to blood flow.
fix: Add to the explanation: "lower the citrate-to-blood-flow ratio, raise effluent or dialysate, or lower the bicarbonate in the fluids".

what: The card front 'Peak ↑ plateau =' reads as a broken sentence on the flash card ('=' meaning unchanged).

Missing high-yield ICU acid–base topics: bicarbonate in septic metabolic acidosis (SSC 2021: suggest bicarbonate when pH ≤ 7.2 with AKI stage 2–3; BICAR-ICU), timing of RRT (STARRT-AKI 2020: no benefit from accelerated start), paired SAT/SBT (ABC trial) and the cuff-leak test with steroids, and oxygen targets in ICU (avoid hyperoxia).
fix: Add bullets or questions to icu-press (bicarbonate), icu-rrt (timing) and icu-wean (SAT+SBT, cuff leak), with sources.

what: The ARDS worked gas has no PEEP, although the lesson says to "record P/F with the PEEP". The interpreter's cause list for this respiratory acidosis offers drive, pump or airways, but not "deliberate low-volume ventilation (permissive hypercapnia)".
fix: Add peep:12 to ex if the engine supports it. In e1.js, when the context is ventilated (fio2 ≥ 0.4 and an ICU lesson or flag), add "permissive hypercapnia on lung-protective settings" to the causes.
